precepts.text: Samson had already taken hold of the two middle pillars and brought Dagon's house down on the lords of the Philistines; they rebuilt this fake god, and the Most High humiliated him again.
precepts.point: They set him in his place again, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning Dagon was fallen on his face again before the ark, with the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him. No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

precepts.why:
“And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood”, and said, “Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein.” Samson had already brought Dagon's house down on the lords of the Philistines. They rebuilt this fake god, and the Most High humiliated him again.

The Philistines had the audacity to bring the ark of God “into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon”, a fake god the Lord had already exposed. When they arose on the morrow, “Dagon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of the Lord.” This was no little souvenir you could knock over; it was a large statue, and nobody had been in there to touch it.

They “set him in his place again”, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning “the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him.” No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day.

precepts.text: He smote his enemies in the hinder parts, and put them to a perpetual reproach; a perpetual embarrassment for taking the ark of the Lord and sitting it beside their idol.
precepts.point: The hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods. Emerods are what we know today as hemorrhoids: swollen veins in the lower rectum that bleed and cause pain. The Most High was not playing games with the heathen; he literally afflicted them in their behinds for stealing the ark.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

precepts.why:
The Psalm tells the same history in one line: “And he smote his enemies in the hinder parts: he put them to a perpetual reproach.” That is what happened at Ashdod. “the hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods.”

Emerods are what we know today as hemorrhoids: swollen veins in the lower rectum that bleed and cause pain. So when the Psalm says the hinder parts, it means exactly that. The Most High was not playing games with the heathen; he literally afflicted them in their behinds for stealing the ark.

And he put them “to a perpetual reproach”: a perpetual embarrassment, for taking the ark of the Lord and sitting it beside their idol.

precepts.text: When the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out that it had been brought to slay them, for the hand of God was heavy there, so the god of Ekron could not even defend his own people against the God of Israel.
precepts.point: When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
When the ark of God was sent to Ekron, “the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.” They begged to send it away, “for there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.”

The god of Ekron could not even defend his own people against the God of Israel. That is Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, the one Ahaziah sent to when he fell through the lattice and was sick.

Ahaziah should have known that history, and it would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron. That is why Elijah asks, “Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron?” He turned to an idol rather than the Most High, and the word came: “thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.”

precepts.text: The Philistines were smitten with emerods for holding the ark and begged Israel to take it away.
precepts.point: The ark blesses when it is with Israel and afflicts those who wrongly hold it, as when the Philistines were struck with emerods for taking it. If it falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it.
precepts.why:
When the Philistines held the ark, “the hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods”. The men of Ashdod said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us: for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god.” They carried it about unto Gath, and there too “the hand of the Lord was against the city with a very great destruction”, and the men “had emerods in their secret parts.” The Philistines begged Israel to take it away.

The ark blesses when it is with Israel and afflicts those who wrongly hold it. After the breach upon Uzza, David was afraid and asked, “How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?” So he carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months, “And the Lord blessed the house of Obed–edom, and all that he had.”

The lesson of Uzza stands: if the ark falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

points: The punishment followed the ark: the hand of the Lord was against Gath with a very great destruction, and he smote the men of the city, both small and great, and they had emerods in their secret parts. Moving it to another city changed nothing; the affliction went with it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

points: By the time they sent the ark to Ekron, the third location, the Ekronites had already heard what was happening and cried out, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

points: The lords of the Philistines were told, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go again to his own place; for there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city, and the hand of God was very heavy there. The men that died not were smitten with the emerods, and the cry of the city went up to heaven. That was the great suffering and affliction the Philistines earned for thinking they had done something by taking the ark.
